open_points.subject: Implementation purity and AdmissionVerdict validity
open_points.text: K-02 now says, “Every promise in these documents that a function repeats itself — equal outputs on equal inputs, a repaired slot staying repaired, a verdict that holds — is a promise about code that obtains neither,” while also saying code obtaining time or chance another way “is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other.” M08 unconditionally says an AdmissionVerdict is “recorded once and then reused, never computed again,” and M09 permits activation or rollback from that admitted verdict.
open_points.question: For an implementation that obtains time or chance through an undetected route, does its recorded admitted verdict remain a valid fact that activation and rollback may reuse, or is admission validity conditional on a purity fact that no model records and the kernel does not detect?
options: The qualification is only a limitation of the product guarantee: the observed verdict remains admitted and reusable for activation and rollback even if later executions vary.
The verdict is valid and reusable only while the implementation obtains neither time nor chance, requiring a modeled eligibility or validity fact and a source that decides it.
Code that obtains time or chance is not eligible to be a function implementation and must be refused, despite the statement that undetected code is judged like any other.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the qualification as non-operational: keep the recorded verdict admitted and reusable because M08 and M09 explicitly require reuse and K-02 says undetected code is judged like any other.

witness.initial: A slot has a contract version with an unchanged nonempty trial corpus. An implementation reads chance through a route the kernel does not detect and can sometimes produce the expected output.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
The kernel runs admission; this execution happens to pass every case, records an admitted verdict and activates the implementation.
A different admitted implementation is later activated for the same contract version.
The agent requests rollback to the earlier chance-dependent implementation while the corpus is still unchanged.
outcomes: Under M08 and M09, the earlier admitted verdict is reused and rollback succeeds; later equal-input runs may nevertheless produce different outputs.

If the new K-02 qualification governs verdict validity, that verdict does not hold for this implementation, so rollback must be refused or admission repeated, although the models contain no fact or action by which the kernel can determine this.
witness.observer: The requesting agent sees rollback succeed or be refused; the owner and trace readers can also see whether subsequent equal-input runs use the earlier implementation and diverge.
